signs.title: Aillwee Cave
signs.text: AILLWEE CAVE. Under the limestone hill of Aillwee in the Burren, County Clare. A local farmer, Jack McGann, found it in 1944 when his dog disappeared down a hole in the rock. It opened to visitors in 1976, and today the tour is about a kilometre of passage.

signs.title: Cave Country
signs.text: The Burren is bare limestone, and rain falls through its cracks instead of running over it. Over a very long time that water carved caves, swallow holes and underground rivers beneath the fields. Much of the Burren's drainage is out of sight.

levers.on: You heave the old iron lever. Somewhere above the steps, a gate swings open.
levers.off: You haul the lever back. The gate clanks shut.

gates.line: A cave gate, locked from the guide's side. There is a big lever by the table.
